snippet.title: Building Tetris with LiveView and OTP
snippet.description:
Who doesn't have fond, nostalgic memories of playing Tetris?

To start 2020, he hosted our webinar with a live coding demonstration of how you can build it yourself, in Elixir, in just over an hour. 

Learn about Phoenix LiveView and how to build applications without JavaScript and see the game built from scratch in this recording.

For the latest Erlang and Elixir blogs, guides, news and webinars visit our website https://www2.erlang-solutions.com/erlangsolutionswebinars

snippet.title: How EMQ x is putting Erlang at the heart of IoT
snippet.description:
EMQ X is massively scalable, highly extensible distributed MQTT message broker written in Erlang/OTP. EMQ X Broker is open source, everyone can use it to build IoT applications. It is currently used by over 5000 enterprise clients, in over 50 countries to connect over 50 million devices.

In this webinar, we explain how EMQ x works, why it is perfect for IoT and demonstrate use cases including smart homes, smart cities and connected cars.

For the latest Erlang and Elixir blogs, guides, news and webinars visit our website https://www2.erlang-solutions.com/erlangsolutionswebinars

snippet.title: Implementing a polyglot microservices architecture | Erlang Solutions Webinar
snippet.description:
Bondy, is an open source networking platform for distributed microservices and IoT applications written in Erlang. It implements the open Web Application Messaging Protocol (WAMP), an open standard TCP and WebSocket protocol that unifies two application messaging patterns: RPC and PubSub. Alejandro Ramallo explains how WAMP works and how it is implemented in Bondy. Most excitingly, he demonstrates how Bondy is used to interconnect the components of an IoT Platform that has been in production for 2 years with hundreds of thousands of connected vehicle and home devices.

WEBINAR LIVE DATE: Wednesday 10 July 2019 | 17:30 GMT / 19:30 CET / 13:30 ET / 10:30 PT

snippet.title: Let’s #TalkConcurrency with Carl Hewitt
snippet.description:
Here is our #TalkConcurrency interview with Carl Hewitt at the Department of Computer Science, Cambridge University.

About Carl Hewitt
Carl has been highly influential in the development of logic, functional and concurrent programming, with his most recognisable work being the Planner (logic programming language) as well as his work on the Actor model of computation.

During his educational years, Carl was at MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), which is famed for its work with science, computing and engineering. Here, he gained his PhD in applied mathematics in 1971 and then continued to work for the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science until 2000 when he became emeritus. 

Interview Date: 07.11.2018
